project.title: Comparative phosphoproteomic analyses of OCT4 protein in hESC
project.projectDescription: This study is directed to systematically map out phosphorylation sites in OCT4 protein that are differentially phosphorylated between naïve hESCs and their primed counterparts, and to further identify the upstream kinases that phosphorylate the sites in naïve hESC-specific manner
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Briefly, the detergent, DTT and IAA in UA buffer were added to block reduced cysteine. Then, the protein suspension was digested with trypsin (Promega, #V5113) at a ratio of 50:1 overnight at 37 °C and collected by centrifugation at 16,000 g for 15 min. Finally, the peptides were desalted with a Sep-Pak C 18 cartridge (Waters, #Z720070) for further analysis. LC-MS/MS was performed on a Q Exactive Plus mass spectrometer coupled with Easy 1200 nLC (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were first loaded to a trap column (100 μm*20 mm, 5 μm, C18) in buffer A (0.1% (v/v) Formic acid in water). Reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) separation was performed with the EASY-nLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) using a self-packed column (75 μm × 150 mm; 3 μm ReproSil-Pur C18 beads, 120 Å, Dr. Maisch GmbH) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. The RP−HPLC mobile phase A was 0.1% formic acid in water, and B was 0.1% formic acid in 95% acetonitrile. Peptides were eluted over 60 min with a linear gradient of buffer B. The gradient was from 2% to 7% B for 3 min, 7% to 35% B for 45 min, 35% to 90% B for 5 min, and maintained at 90% B for 7 min. Data were acquired by DDA with a Q Exactive Plus mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). The analysis was set at positive ion mode and the duration was 60 min. Scan range: 300-1800 m/z, MS 1 resolution: 70,000 @m/z 200, AGC target: 1e6, MS 1 maximum IT: 50 ms, MS2 resolution: 17,500 @ m/z 200, AGC target: 1e5, MS 2 maximum IT: 50 ms, MS2 activation type: HCD, Isolation window: 2.0 Th, Normalized collision energy:27.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: We processed the mass spectra using MaxQuant software version 1.6.0.16. MS data were searched against the Swissprot Homo sapiens_20422_201905 31.fasta (20,422 total entries). The trypsin was selected as the digestion enzyme. The maximal two missed cleavage sites and the mass tolerance of 4.5 ppm for precursor ions and 20 ppm for fragment ions were defined for database search. The database search results were filtered and exported with <1% false discovery rate (FDR) at peptide-spectrum-matched level, and protein level, respectively. For phosphorylation data searching, phosphorylation on serine, threonine, and tyrosine was added into the searching parameter and the site localization probability was set as > 0.75.
